request.spec:
A person can be retired from a date (defaults to the sheet's today). A claim dated after a person's
retirement date is refused with an error; claims dated on or before it are allowed even if added
later. Retired people are left out of the list (no row for them on the screen at all) unless "show
retired" is on: a toggle on the screen, off when the screen is first opened and left as it is by
loading a sheet. Their claims keep counting in every total. Show retired yes/no and retired-from.
Retiring writes PERSON_RETIRED name=<name> from=<date>. A person with a retirement date set counts
as retired at once, whatever the date, even one after the sheet's today: the row shows retired yes,
the list hides it, and every rule that speaks of a retired person or member applies to them.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person can be retired from a date (defaults to the sheet's today). A claim dated after a person's
retirement date is refused with an error; claims dated on or before it are allowed even if added
later. Retired people are left out of the list (no row for them on the screen at all) unless "show
retired" is on: a toggle on the screen, off when the screen is first opened and left as it is by
loading a sheet. Their claims keep counting in every total. Show retired yes/no and retired-from.
Retiring writes PERSON_RETIRED name=<name> from=<date>. A person with a retirement date set counts
as retired at once, whatever the date, even one after the sheet's today: the row shows retired yes,
the list hides it, and every rule that speaks of a retired person or member applies to them.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People can now be retired from a date, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the retire spec.

**What it does**
- **Stored data:** a new migration (`V16__person_retired.sql`) adds a nullable `retired_from` date to each person. If the date is set, the person counts as retired straight away, even if the date is after the sheet's today.
- **Retiring:** a new endpoint, `PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/retire`, takes `{ "date": … }`. A blank date means the sheet's today, and a date that isn't a real calendar date is refused. It writes `PERSON_RETIRED sheet=… by=… name=… from=…` to the audit file. Retiring doesn't change any totals, so no ROLLUP line is written, which matches what the spec expects.
- **Claim rule:** a claim dated after the person's retirement date is refused; one dated on or before it still goes through. The check covers:
  - adding a claim from the person's row;
  - quick-add, since it uses the same code to create the claim;
  - editing a claim to a later date. The request only mentions adding claims, so this part is my reading of it.
- **Screen:**
  - Each person row has a new cell with `person-retired` (yes/no), `person-retired-from`, a date box, a Retire button and a `person-error` message.
  - A `show-retired` checkbox above the list hides retired people entirely when it's off. Its setting is kept in the URL, so it starts off when the screen opens and loading a sheet doesn't change it.
  - Totals still count every person's claims, retired or not.

**Worth knowing**
- There's no way to set a retirement date back to empty yet. Retiring someone who is already retired just changes their date.
- Retiring a person also bumps their version number. If someone has that person's editor open at the time, their save will be refused as a conflict and the form will reload the current values.
